text:
alex: heads up — noticed a ~20% p99 bump on canary after yesterday's prefix rebalance. correlates with a spike in prefix cache evictions around 03:40 UTC.

maria: oh no. can you paste the canary id and the failing job?

alex: canary id canary-20260312-07, deploy sha abc1234. quick numbers from the metric query:
```
prefix_cache_evictions_total{env="canary"} = +4.8k (03:30-04:00)
request_p99_ms{route="gen"}= 124 -> 150
cache_hit_rate_prefix = 0.62 -> 0.48
```

dylan: thanks. do you have a perf profile or heap dump?

alex: uploaded a pprof to the run at https://perf.redwood/canary-20260312-07/profile.tar.gz — looks like many small evictions and short-lived KV allocs.

june: scheduler logs show a burst of shard moves at 03:35, probably the rebalance TTL policy kicked in when hotset shifted. I can dig rack-level timing.

kevin: curious if this is fragmentation vs eviction policy mismatch. last week we enabled adaptive-ttl with threshold 0.2 — maybe it's too aggressive for this workload.

maria: can we reproduce locally with the microbench? alex, can you drop the exact bench command you used?

alex: sure — run this to reproduce approximate profile:
```
./scripts/kv_microbench --mode=canary-like --qps=250 --duration=600 \
  --prefix-dist=zipf(1.2) --shard-moves=enabled --trace-output=out/pprof
```

dylan: I'll run that with sampling and allocator flamegraphs, will try sample-rate 100k and `jemalloc_conf` toggles. will share flamegraphs in ~40m.

june: I'll pull scheduler traces and check whether shard moves are clustered by node. if they are, we may need to stagger rebalances.

maria: quick ask — can someone open a tiny config PR to tone the adaptive-ttl down to 0.15 and add a canary flag? i can review/test.

alex: opened draft PR: https://git.redwood/repo/infra#4321. PR notes: change adaptive_ttl_threshold: 0.2 -> 0.15 + guard to avoid >3 shard moves per min.

kevin: good. i'll run a quick offline sim to estimate hit-rate impact before we push.

perf-bot: deploy canary-20260312-07 finished at 2026-03-12T03:29:18Z :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks all. let's treat this as a perf regression until proven otherwise. keep updates here. if dylan or june find a smoking gun, ping me and i'll prioritize the PR. :thumbsup:

dylan: uploaded flamegraphs to the ticket and linked them in PR comments. initial impression: evictions are dominated by <1KB entries, many due to rehashed prefixes after shard moves.

june: scheduler traces show majority of moves initiated by node-allocator on node-7 and node-11 within a 70s window. adding jitter on rebalances seems like a quick mitigation.

alex: noted. i'll add experiment notes and run the microbench with PR config to confirm. will post final numbers here.

maria: if we don't see improvement in 2 runs, let's revert the rebalance enable flag for canary only and hold until patch.

alex: on it. thanks everyone — will post results in ~90m. :coffee:
